description:
Here is a number no doctor ever told you: if you're in the bottom quartile of fitness for your age, your risk of dying is HIGHER than a smoker's — and almost nobody in medicine has ever measured yours.

That's the crack in the foundation Peter Attia builds "Outlive: The Science & Art of Longevity" on. In this deep dive we break down his whole framework in plain language: why modern medicine optimizes for the wrong finish line, the Four Horsemen of slow death (heart disease, cancer, neurodegeneration, type 2 diabetes), why apoB — not your standard cholesterol panel — is the real driver of heart disease, the insulin-resistance "sick soil" every chronic disease grows in, and the Centenarian Decathlon: deciding what you want your body to do at 85 and reverse-engineering the training now. Plus VO2 max, strength and grip, Nutrition 3.0's three levers, sleep as the brain's dishwasher — and the emotional-health chapter Attia almost cut, where the ultimate optimizer realized his own family flinched when he walked in.

The finish line was never "don't die." It's whether the last decade is worth living — and you have to train for your marginal decade starting today. No fluff, no fabricated facts.
